draft.title: A sophisticated thesis
card: A thesis is the main claim of an essay. It answers the question and sets the direction for every paragraph that follows.
it names a theme or technique and stops there. Almost any reader of the text would already agree with it.
it shows tension, change or complexity in the text. It may say how an ending complicates what came before, or how a theme is tested rather than simply shown.
Words such as although, yet, while and by the end often help a thesis show complexity. A thesis can be built like this: the text seems to say X, but it also shows Y.
draft.remember: A sophisticated thesis argues how or why an idea is complicated, not just that the idea is there.

a.q: Which thesis about an invented novel, The Salt Road, is the most sophisticated?
opts: Although the novel praises return, its ending shows home as changed
The Salt Road explores the theme of home through its main character
The author uses vivid imagery to show the character misses home
The novel shows that home matters and that leaving it is hard
a.why: The first option shows tension: the novel praises return, yet its ending complicates that idea. The second is tempting because it names a theme and a character, but it only states a topic and makes no argument about complexity.
a.clue: Look for the claim that shows the text pulling in two directions.

b.q: Priya is writing about an invented play, Low Tide, in which a family keeps a secret that is revealed in the last scene. Which thesis best shows how an ending can complicate what came before?
opts: The revelation makes the family's earlier warmth both real and a cover
The revelation at the end of the play shocks the audience
The play uses a secret to explore family and the pain of lies
The family's secret is revealed in the last scene after being hidden
b.why: The first option argues that the ending changes how earlier scenes read, so the warmth holds two meanings at once. The second is tempting because it mentions the ending, but it only describes an effect on the audience and shows no complexity in the ideas.
b.clue: Which thesis changes how we read the earlier scenes?
